evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation of both intronic and 3' UTR binding on the same transcripts.

claim: Hrb27c protein binds to and is required for localization of Grk mRNA in Drosophila.
source_text: and the observation that the predominantly nuclear Hrb27c protein (whose mammalian homologue is the DAZAP1 splicing factor; (Goina et al., 2008)) also binds to and is required for localization of Grk mRNA
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the cited study (Goodrich et al., 2004).

claim: ZBP1 binds to actin mRNA in the nucleus and is required for its localization.
source_text: In mammalian cells, ZBP1 binds to actin mRNA in the nucleus and subsequently is required for its localization
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the cited studies (Gu et al., 2002; Pan et al., 2007).

claim: NOVA binds to GlyRα2 transcripts in introns to regulate alternative splicing and is also associated with 3' UTR and localization of the same mRNA in the neuronal dendrite.
source_text: and NOVA binds to transcripts (e.g. GlyRα2) in introns to regulate alternative splicing and is also associated with 3′ UTR and localization of the same mRNA in the neuronal dendrite
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the cited study (Racca et al., 2010).

claim: Intronic NOVA binding to high affinity intronic clusters would allow a high local concentration of the protein upon individual transcripts.
source_text: For example, intronic NOVA binding to high affinity intronic clusters would allow a high local concentration of the protein upon individual transcripts, potentially allowing rearrangement in cis and binding of additional secondary RNA elements, including those within the 3′ UTR.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative model proposed to explain the observed binding patterns.

claim: Local concentration and one-dimensional rearrangements in cis play an important role in scanning and initiation of transcription.
source_text: it is noteworthy that such local concentration and one-dimensional rearrangements in cis are believed to play an important role in scanning and initiation of transcription
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from studies on transcription cited in the manuscript.

claim: NOVA localization changes after seizure.
source_text: In this context, it is especially notable that NOVA localization changes after seizure
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence microscopy in this study.

claim: The association of NOVA with newly transcribed and spliced transcripts may be coupled in an activity-sensitive manner with their localization and/or translational control.
source_text: suggesting that the association of NOVA with newly transcribed and spliced transcripts may be coupled in an activity-sensitive manner with their localization and/or translational control
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference based on the observed activity-dependent changes in NOVA localization.

claim: HITS-CLIP provides a powerful means of providing unambiguous and unbiased sites of RNA–protein interaction.
source_text: However, HITS-CLIP provides a powerful means of providing unambiguous and unbiased sites of RNA–protein interaction.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the HITS-CLIP method.

claim: Directed analysis of unbiased HITS-CLIP targets can reveal cryptic biology.
source_text: Directed analysis of unbiased HITS-CLIP targets can reveal cryptic biology, as in the analysis of developmental HITS-CLIP maps to study NOVA interactions with transcripts of the Reelin pathway and thereby identify a previously unknown NOVA-dependent alternative exon necessary for proper neuronal migration
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the cited study (Yano et al., 2010).

claim: Changes in electrical activity affect the distribution of Nova.
source_text: Collectively, our data support a model in which changes in electrical activity affect the distribution of Nova
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the seizure-induced changes in NOVA localization.

claim: Changes in Nova distribution alter the splicing of cryptic exons that elicit NMD.
source_text: altering the splicing of cryptic exons that elicit NMD
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the combination of NOVA relocalization and NMD exon regulation after seizure.

claim: Changes in NMD exon splicing may provide a homeostatic means of regulating levels of transcripts and proteins associated with epilepsy.
source_text: these changes may provide a homeostatic means of regulating levels of transcripts and proteins associated with epilepsy
evidence_reasoning: This is a model proposed based on the combined data from this study.
